subject: Energy
title: Springs and Elastic Storage
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Springs and Elastic Storage.

hook.text: Mechanical springs store energy through deformation—centuries-old technology in clocks and wind-up devices.

buildup.text: Compressed springs release energy predictably—the force is proportional to displacement (Hooke's Law).

discovery.text: Modern elastomeric storage uses advanced rubber-like materials—stretching and releasing to capture small energy bursts.

twist.text: Energy density in springs is extremely low—useful for small devices but impractical for grid-scale applications.

climax.text: Some researchers combine springs with regenerative braking—recovering energy from elevators and industrial machinery.

punchline.text: Wind it up, let it go—the oldest stored energy trick.

quiz.question: Why aren't springs used for grid-scale energy storage?
